The Great Learning on self

The Great Learning appears in this archive through verified English quotations that touch self. To ask about the self is to ask what persists through experience, what can be known from the first-person point of view, and how character is formed. Some traditions treat the self as a substantial soul; others as a stream of experience, a social role, or a practical center of agency. Read the passages as entry points, then return to the full thinker and theme pages for wider context.

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the The Great Learning thinker page for biography and to the self theme for other voices on the same question.
